shared_elements: pale weathered limestone surface with carved/incised decoration
band of repeated motifs running parallel to the upper edge
row of arc / loop (arch-like) shapes near the top
sets of parallel incised lines used as framing
hatched or net-like fill (grid squares in A, cross-hatched band in B)
a broad main field below the upper band
justification: The most specific correspondence is the layout: in both, a horizontal register of repeated arc/loop forms and hatched or lined banding runs along the top edge, above a larger open field carrying the principal motifs, with parallel incised lines acting as framing. The biggest difference is content and technique: A is wholly abstract, shallow linear incision (nested arcs, two grid rectangles, a U-shaped form), while B is modelled low relief dominated by recognisable animals in profile and plant forms, so beyond the generic banded scheme and the stone medium they share little.
